correctness.rationale: For every bounded bilinear map, both Arens extensions are norm-preserving linear extensions. Hence the discrepancy operator \(D(h)=h^{\square}-h^{\diamond}\) is linear with norm at most \(2\), giving the \(2\)-Lipschitz estimate by the reverse triangle inequality and the distance lower bound by comparison with any regular product. In the sharpness algebra on \(\ell_1\oplus_1\ell_1\oplus_1\mathbb C\), the multiplication has norm \(1\) and every triple product is zero. Free-ultrafilter functionals applied to the triangular sign matrix give the two iterated limits \(1\) and \(-1\), so the Arens gap is at least \(2\) and therefore exactly \(2\). The zero product is regular at distance \(1\), proving sharpness of both constants.

value.rationale: The focal perturbation result is qualitative and witness-dependent. The norm gap \(\Delta_A\) turns Arens irregularity into a canonical metric obstruction: it gives an explicit exclusion radius from every regular associative multiplication and is stable with the best possible universal constant. The cube-zero sharpness example shows the estimate is not a proof artifact. This is a structural quantitative refinement, not a parameter substitution or finite recomputation.
